problems.title: Design a Parking Lot
problems.description:
Design an automated multi-floor parking lot system for urban commercial buildings.

Key Requirements:
- Support multiple vehicle types (Car, Bike, Truck) with designated spot sizes per floor.
- Track available and occupied spots per floor in real-time.
- Issue entry tickets with spot assignment and timestamp; calculate fees on exit based on duration.
- Gracefully handle full lot edge cases when no spots are available.

What a good submission should cover:
Your design should show how vehicles get matched to spots, how the system tracks occupancy, and how fees are calculated for different vehicle types.

problems.title: Design an Elevator System
problems.description:
Design a smart elevator control system managing multi-car dispatching in a high-rise building.

Key Requirements:
- Control multiple elevators across multiple floors.
- Process internal destination buttons and external floor hall requests (up/down).
- Efficiently dispatch requests to optimal elevators to minimize wait times.
- Manage movement states (Idle, Moving Up, Moving Down), door logic, and queue priorities.

What a good submission should cover:
Your design should cover request dispatching logic, state transitions, queue handling, and class relationships between controllers, floors, and elevators.

attempts.submissionText:
Parking Lot Design

Here are the main classes I've designed for this system:

Vehicle — a base class/interface with licensePlate and vehicleType properties. Car, Bike, and Truck classes extend Vehicle, since each vehicle type has a different size and needs a different kind of spot.

Spot — represents a single parking spot. It has spotId, spotType (Small, Medium, Large), floorNumber, and isOccupied (boolean). Each Spot has a SpotType that determines which vehicles can fit into it — for example, a Bike can only park in a Small spot, and a Truck needs a Large spot.

Slot — represents a group/section of spots within a floor. A Slot contains multiple Spot objects. This makes it easier to manage how many spots are free on a given floor, without having to check every individual spot.

ParkingLot — this is the main controller class for the whole system. It contains multiple floors, and each floor contains multiple Slots. ParkingLot is responsible for:

Finding an available Spot when a vehicle enters (based on vehicle type)
Allocating the Spot and marking it as occupied
Freeing the Spot when the vehicle exits
Generating a Ticket at entry time

Ticket — created when a vehicle enters the lot. It stores ticketId, vehicle details, the assigned spot, and entryTime. At exit, the same Ticket is used to record exitTime and calculate the fee.

FeeCalculator — a separate class/interface responsible only for calculating the parking fee, based on the difference between entryTime and exitTime, with different rates depending on vehicle type (a Truck's rate will be higher than a Bike's). I kept this as a separate class so that if the fee formula needs to change later (e.g. from hourly to daily pricing), only this class needs to be modified — the rest of the system stays untouched.

How the flow works:

A vehicle enters → ParkingLot searches for a free Spot matching its vehicle type
The Spot is allocated and isOccupied is set to true
A Ticket is generated with the entryTime
The vehicle exits → the Ticket is used to free up the Spot
FeeCalculator computes the fee based on entry and exit time

Design decisions:

Vehicle was made an interface/base class so new vehicle types (like Bus) can be added easily without changing existing code — this supports extensibility
FeeCalculator was kept separate so that pricing logic changes don't affect the rest of the system
Spot and Slot were kept as separate classes to keep floor-level and spot-level management clean and not mixed together
